events.name: The Kind Stranger
events.intro: The path's forked three times, and the third fork looks like the first. A man in a very good suit is coming the other way, with a walking stick, as if it's a park. The stranger: "You've gone round twice. So did I, the first time; it's the oak. Everybody turns at the oak. Is that one poisoned? Here." An Antidote, from an inside pocket. He crouches to give it himself, without minding the suit. "What's its name? ...And did it choose you, or you it? ...Ah. That's the better way round."

success.text: "A man out for a walk." He smiles. It's a real one. He asks about each of your Pokémon, with real interest, and listens to the answers: where it was met, what it's good at, what it's afraid of. Of whichever's weakest: "That one'll surprise you. The ones that start behind have further to go. I've always thought further was the point." He shows you the way out past the oak. He doesn't give his name.

events.name: Visitors
events.intro: A town with no clocks. No kettles. A bicycle with no bell. Your bag is one item lighter. Something's been taken. You'll get it back. A man in a hat made of foil, Mr. Oswald Peake: "It's them. I've said for years. They take metal. They take things that tick. Do you know what ticks? Ships. I'm not frightened. I'm thrilled."

success.text: Small round footprints. A dropped teaspoon. A cave, the next node on.

events.name: Visitors: The Cave
events.intro: Inside: Clefairy, dozens, in a chain, passing things hand to hand. In the middle, as high as a house: kettles, clocks, a weathervane, a bathtub, a bicycle bell at the very top, all fitted together into something with fins. One of them's holding your item up against a gap, to see if it fits. It doesn't. It hands it back, politely, and takes a doorknob instead. It launches whether or not you interfere.

success.text: A sound like every kettle in town coming to the boil at once. It goes up. It really does. It comes down again, in the pond, gently. They climb out, wet, and look at the sky, and start collecting kettles. Your item comes back, and a Comet Shard, and a Clefairy that's decided to stay on the ground asks to come.

effects.text: Watched the Clefairy's kettle ship go up, and come down in the pond.

events.name: Triage
events.intro: A lorry on its side on the coast road. Nobody's badly hurt; it's said at once. A queue of shaken Pokémon and their people outside a door marked DR. PROCTOR. HUMANS. Dr. Proctor: "The Center's full. They've sent them to me. I do people. I've a Chansey; she does the Pokémon in the waiting room for fun. I don't know which end of a Weepinbell is the front. You're a trainer. Stand there. Tell me who's first."

success.text: The first patient.
"Nor am I, for these. Stand there."

events.intro: A Dodrio, one head drooping. The other two heads are holding it up.

success.text: Right. That saves time for the next.
It costs nobody anything but minutes.

events.name: The Building Site
events.intro: An empty lot. An old man. A Machop, stamping. The old man: "I'm getting my land ready for a building." Stamp. Stamp. The Machop moves one pace left. Stamp. Flat earth.

success.text: "A good one."
"Not long. Since the war."
Your Fighting type goes over. It stamps beside the Machop. They don't speak. They fall into step. A little experience, and Bond +1.

events.name: The Building Site: Nearly Ready
events.intro: The same lot, in the same run, a long way on. Flat earth. The old man: "Nearly ready." Stamp. Stamp.

success.text: "A good one. Nearly."
Your Fighting type remembers the step. It stamps beside the Machop. They don't speak. They fall into step. A little experience, and Bond +1.

events.name: The Rival in the Tower
events.intro: The third floor. Somebody's standing among the stones with their back to the stairs. It's the rival. They don't turn round. Their eyes are open. Their Pokémon are out, all of them, fighting hard, at empty air. The rival's lips are moving. They're calling moves. Their voice isn't quite theirs. The rival's lead sees you. It's exhausted. It looks at you the way something looks when it's been waiting for anyone at all.

success.text: They blink. The air in front of their Pokémon's just air.
They turn, slowly, and it isn't them looking.
The rival's team, commanded by something that doesn't know them: it uses moves they'd never pick. Beating it lets go.
Your lead stands beside it. It's your lead's cry that reaches them.

events.name: The Rival in the Tower: Not Them
events.intro: Something that doesn't know them is calling the moves.

success.text: The rival's team, commanded by something that doesn't know them: it uses moves they'd never pick. Beating it lets go.

events.name: The Rival in the Tower: After
events.intro: The cold goes out of the floor.

success.text: Rival: "What... why are we... how long have I been up here?" They look at their Pokémon. They can see what state they're in. "...I did that. Didn't I. I was telling them to." They don't remember it clearly, and they're embarrassed anyway. They hold out the Silph Scope they came in with: "Take it. I don't want to see what was standing next to me. You look."

effects.text: Brought the rival back from among the stones on the third floor.

events.name: The Festival of Dolls
events.intro: The Store, and a crowd that's all elbows. Banners: PRINCESS FESTIVAL. EVERYTHING NEARLY FREE. Miss Stott's lift is carrying nineteen people and a rug. Miss Stott: "Third! Discs! Mind the... madam, that's a person, not a step!" Shop prices are halved for this visit. On the roof: a four-battle knockout. The prize: a set of antique dolls on seven tiers. Jessie's entered. No disguise. Her own name. She's standing in front of the dolls, and she isn't scheming. James, to you, low: "She never had any. Not one. There was a year they ate snow. Don't... she'd hate that I said."

success.text: Your name goes on the board, opposite hers.
Everything nearly free.

success.text: Round 1. No items.

success.text: The final.

events.name: The Festival of Dolls: The Dolls
events.intro: You won. The dolls, on their seven tiers.

success.text: She doesn't take them. Then she does. She holds the smallest one in both hands. Jessie: "I don't... what do you want? ...Nothing. You want nothing. I don't know what face to do." Meowth: "That one, Jess. That one's fine."

events.name: The Secret House
events.intro: From the gate, on a clear day: a roof, at the very back of the reserve. Mr. Lowe, at the gate: "There's a prize, if you get there on one ticket. Nobody does. They see a Chansey and that's that." Five hundred steps. Four hundred of them are just walking; the rest are what you spend them on.

events.intro: The count on your ticket.

events.name: The Shell on the Tail
events.intro: A rock pool. A Slowpoke with its tail in it. A professor on a camp stool, watching the tail, with a notebook open at a blank page. Professor Westwood the Fifth: "My great-great-grandfather asked: why does it evolve when the Shellder bites? He didn't find out. Nor did his son. Nor his. Nor my father. They're all on the wall at home. Looking at me." He's brought the portraits. They're propped along the rocks. Four men with the same nose, increasingly disappointed. "I've had this one's tail in that pool since April. The Shellder won't bite."

success.text: He writes that down, then crosses it out. The trio arrive, after the Slowpoke. A battle starts that isn't yours: Jessie's Shellder, thrown; the Slowpoke, slow; the professor on his feet. The Shellder misses. It lands on the tail. It bites, out of habit. Light. A Slowbro's standing in the pool. It's upright. It looks at its own hands. Professor Westwood: "It's the balance. The weight on the tail. It has to stand up to carry it. And standing... it thinks better standing. They help each other stand. It was never the bite. It's the..." He's stopped. He's looked at the notebook. He's looked at the portraits. "...Oh. That's it, then. That's all of it. What do I do on Monday?"

events.name: Where It Was Happy
events.intro: A wood. Movement in every tree. They come out, one at a time: thirty, forty, all of them the same kind as your lead. Your lead goes still. It's never seen another one. It's never seen this many of anything like itself. One comes forward. They touch noses. And then it's in among them, and it's gone, and it's all one sound. All day, you watch from a log. It's playing. It's teaching a small one something. It's never, in this whole run, looked like that. Evening. The fire. Your lead's asleep in a heap of its own kind. One of them's got an arm over it.

success.text: The path. The trees thinning. You don't look back. You're doing very well at not looking back. Behind you: something running. Fast, and not stopping. It hits you in the chest and holds on. At the tree line, all of them have come out to see it off. They're cheering. They knew before you did.

effects.text: Tried to leave your lead where it was happy. It came after you. It always will.

success.text: Nothing changes. Morning. It's on your bag, ready. It was never going to stay.
Nothing changes. Morning. It's on your bag, ready. It was never going to stay.

events.name: The Training Course
events.intro: You're on the ground. Six Growlithe are sitting on you. It's very warm. Officer Jenny: "Hold! ...Oh. You're not him. He's got a moustache. I'm sorry. They go for the bag; you've a burglar's bag. Off. Off. All six. Let me make it up to you: want to run one of yours through the course?"

success.text: The wall first.
"Fair." She helps you up. The Growlithe help, too, mostly by licking.

events.name: The Training Course: The Wall
events.intro: A timing jump.

success.text: Over.

events.name: The Training Course: The Tunnel
events.intro: A dark crawl: you call left and right.

success.text: Out the far end, dusty.

events.name: The Training Course: The Voice
events.intro: You breathe helium and shout a command in a squeak. A Growlithe that only knows the voice wouldn't obey.

success.text: It tilts its head. It sniffs. It looks at you as if to say: I know it's you; why are you doing that? And it does it. Passed. An officer's whistle: the next police encounter in the region is friendly.

effects.text: Passed Officer Jenny's course with a squeak.

success.text: It does the first two and sits down at the third, puzzled. Jenny: "It's Bond, not brains. Come back when it's had longer with you."

events.name: The Old Street
events.intro: A film town: billboards, palm trees, a street of theatres. The trio's on it. Meowth's stopped walking. Jessie: "What?" Meowth: "Nothin'. Go on. I'll catch yous up." They go. He doesn't follow. He's looking down an alley. He's seen you. He doesn't run. Meowth: "...I used to eat outta that bin. That one. Best bin on the street."

success.text: He doesn't stop you.

events.name: The Old Street: The Alley
events.intro: The alley: a gang of street Meowth. A Persian on a crate. They know him. They circle him. They don't speak. One of them mimes walking on two legs, and falls about. A window above: a cat on a cushion, with a ribbon. Meowth, not looking up: "Meowzie. She said I wasn't good enough. Said she liked people. Rich ones, that talk nice. So I learned. Standin' up. Took a month; I fell down a lot. Then talkin'. Out of a picture book. First word I got was 'rocket.' That's the only reason I'm in this line o' work. I come back. On two feet. I said, 'Meowzie, I can speak, I can walk, I'm just like a person.' And she said that made me a freak."

success.text: You walk into the alley and stand at his shoulder. That's all. The Persian looks at you. It looks at Meowth. Nobody's ever stood there before. It gets down off the crate, and goes. In the window, the cat's watching. Meowth looks up at last. Meowth: "Nah. Y'know what? I talk. I'm the only one there is. She can keep the cushion." And then: "Don't tell them two I was here."

effects.text: Stood beside Meowth in the alley where he learned to talk.

events.name: Inside the Machine
events.intro: A Center where the transfer machine eats Poké Balls. A queue of worried trainers. An engineer with a helmet that's all wires. Dr. Akihabara: "They go in. They don't come out the other end. Something's in the line. I can send a person in to look. It's quite safe. I think it's quite safe. I've a guide." A Porygon. It bobs. (Staged without flashing: steady colours, slow fades.)

success.text: Corridors of steady light.
The queue sighs.

events.name: Inside the Machine: The Toll Booth
events.intro: The trio, with a Porygon of their own and a roadblock made of stolen Balls. James: "It's a toll booth! In a telephone! It's the perfect crime!"

success.text: The trio.

events.name: Inside the Machine: The Anti-Virus
events.intro: A shape that can't tell thieves from visitors. It can't be beaten for long; it regrows.

success.text: It comes apart, and starts to come back together.

success.text: A turn.

events.name: Snowed In

remembers.notice: Your Fire type lies across the door. The night's easy.

events.intro: A mountain road. Snow from the side. The path's gone, then the hill's gone, then your hand. A drift, hollowed out. A cave the size of a cupboard. The fire's lit, and it's small. The party's out, all of them, crowded in. They're shivering. It's warmer in the Balls. You know it.

choices.label: "In. All of you. That's not a request."

success.text: They go. One by one. The light of each Ball closing. The cave's very quiet. The fire's lower. A Ball opens by itself. Then another. Then all of them. They're back, packed in round you, the big ones on the outside, your lead under your coat. Nobody's looking at you. It's been decided. Morning. Blue sky. The drift's a white dome with a hole at the top, and steam coming out of it.

effects.text: Snowed in, and nobody would go in their Balls.

events.name: The Bicycle Race
events.intro: A town with bunting. A start line. A rule, on a board: THE RIDER'S LEAD POKÉMON MUST BE ON THE BICYCLE. Your lightest Pokémon hops up at once. Your heaviest looks at it. It looks at the bicycle. It looks at you, with hope.

success.text: Light: fast uphill, twitchy downhill.
Heavy: very slow uphill. Downhill, unstoppable. Literally: the brakes don't count.
The front wheel's flat by the first corner. It's holding your shoulders. It's having the best day.

events.name: The Bicycle Race: Uphill

success.text: The crowd's favourite. They've waited at the line. A year of free food at the finish-line diner: a full rest, now, and again whenever you pass this way this run.

events.name: The Gamblers
events.intro: Three men at a folding table by the road, each with a coin, none of them doing anything until it's landed. The coin decides his lead and his opening move. You may call it. Rich: "Heads, I fight. Tails, I fight worse."

choices.label: Call it. (A right call picks his lead.)

success.text: The coin's fair, and it's said so. Rich's battle.

failure.text: The coin's fair, and it's said so. Rich's battle.

success.text: The coin's fair, and it's said so. Rich's battle.
He flips for whether to be offended. It comes up "no."

events.name: The Gamblers: All Three
events.intro: All three beaten.

success.text: Dirk: "It's the one I've been flipping. It's lucky. Not for me." An Amulet Coin.

effects.text: Beat all three gamblers on the road. Dirk paid up with his coin.

success.text: Coins, doubled.

events.name: The Gamblers: Done
events.intro: Dirk pockets his coin.

success.text: "Flip you for it next time."

events.name: The Fame Checker
events.intro: It listens to what people say about people. "Brock? Cooks for ten. Never sits down himself." A Pewter grandmother. "Erika fell asleep judging the flower show. Gave first prize to a hedge." A Celadon gardener. "The man at Viridian's Gym is never in. Lovely suits, the once I saw him." The Old Man.

success.text: Each remark fills a line in the Notebook.

effects.text: Got the Fame Checker from Miss Pennyfeather.

events.name: The Vs. Seeker
events.intro: A woman at the Center's counter, Miss Leonora Pennyfeather: "I don't use these now. I've a shop. This one finds people who'd like another go at you. This one listens to what people say about people. Mind what you do with the second."

success.text: The Vs. Seeker, and the Fame Checker. A rematched trainer, later: "You! I've been practising. I've been practising specifically you."

events.name: Lost and Found
events.intro: A gatehouse with a guard who won't let anyone through. Beside it, steps going down. A man coming up: "Long way. Dark. People drop things. I dropped a sandwich in '94. If you find it, don't."

success.text: A long walk by the light of your lead. It stops twice: two things somebody dropped.
It stops three times.

events.name: Lost and Found: The Far End
events.intro: A girl on the bottom step, Saige: "Are you a trade? I'm waiting for a trade. Mum said wait here. That was a while ago. I've a Nidoran. He's called Mr. Nido. I'd like a girl one." The Honest Trade Card is shown.

choices.label: Trade her a Nidoran (female) for Mr. Nido.

success.text: Saige, after: "Be nice to Mr. Nido. He doesn't like the dark. That's why we waited where the light comes down." Bond grows half again as fast, as with every trade.

effects.text: Traded for Mr. Nido at the bottom of the Underground Path.

choices.label: "I haven't one. I'll sit with you a bit."

success.text: You sit where the light comes down. Her mum comes, eventually, with chips.

events.name: The Swimmers' Relay
events.intro: Open water. Four buoys in a line to the horizon. Heads bobbing between them, shouting. A swimmer, treading water: "Buoy to buoy! Battle at each! Last one to four buys the chips! You've got something that floats?"

choices.label: Ride one that can carry you.

success.text: Strokes, in rhythm, to the first buoy.
"Chips are on you, then!"

events.name: The Swimmers' Relay: Buoy 1
events.intro: Buoy 1, and a swimmer hanging off it.

success.text: A battle at the buoy.
Coins for each buoy. Chips, on the beach, after. Everybody's buying everybody's.

events.name: The Swimmers' Relay: Buoy 2
events.intro: Buoy 2, and a swimmer hanging off it.

success.text: A battle at the buoy.
Coins for each buoy. Chips, on the beach, after. Everybody's buying everybody's.

events.intro: Buoy three. "I'm not out of breath. I'm pacing. ...Give me a second. Then battle."

success.text: A battle at the buoy.

events.intro: First to the last buoy.

success.text: A Mystic Water or a Wave Incense, and a tired, pleased Pokémon. Chips, on the beach, after. Everybody's buying everybody's.

effects.text: First to the last buoy in the Swimmers' Relay.

events.name: The Aides: Miss Ione Tack
events.intro: A gatehouse before the Gym's approach. A woman with a clipboard. She doesn't say who she works for, and doesn't send you anywhere.

success.text: Miss Ione Tack: "Ten. That's the first hurdle. Most people have ten by accident." A lamp, for the dark routes.

effects.text: An Aide counted your 10.

success.text: "Come back with more. I'll be here. It's a gatehouse. Where would I go."

events.name: The Aides: Mr. Humphrey Tack
events.intro: Another gatehouse, another clipboard.

success.text: Mr. Humphrey Tack: "Twenty! My brother wanted thirty. He's always been unreasonable." An Exp. Share.

effects.text: An Aide counted your 20.

success.text: "Come back with more. I'll be here. It's a gatehouse. Where would I go."

events.name: The Aides: Old Mrs. Tack
events.intro: A gatehouse with a cushion on the chair.

success.text: Old Mrs. Tack: "Forty. I've three children in gatehouses. None of them write. Count yours for me, dear." An Amulet Coin.

effects.text: An Aide counted your 40.

success.text: "Come back with more. I'll be here. It's a gatehouse. Where would I go."

events.name: The Joyful Game Corner
events.intro: The three machines are pushed back against the wall. The floor's chalked with squares. The owner: "She said they were boring. The machines. She's six. She's right. So: these."

success.text: A rope, turned by a Machop. A rhythm; it speeds up. Lostelle counts, wrongly. Lostelle: "Yours is good. Mine's better. Mine's imaginary. It never trips." Berries, by score. Bond +1, once.

choices.label: Berry-picking (a Doduo or Dodrio: more than one head).

success.text: A tree, three heads, three baskets. Each head's steered separately. They argue. Lostelle: "Yours is good. Mine's better. Mine's imaginary. It never trips." Berries, by score. Bond +1, once.
No coins. No prizes but Berries, by score.
Back along the jetty.

events.name: Treasure Beach
events.intro: A beach nobody's on. The sea's gone out a long way, and left things. Your lead digs. It's found something. It brings it over very carefully, as if it knows.

success.text: Pearls, a Star Piece, shells.
Pearls, a Star Piece, shells, and two more.
Back along the jetty.

events.name: The Lady of the Resort
events.intro: A veranda. A parasol. A young lady who's seen everything on the island twice. Selphy: "I'm bored. It's a medical condition; I've had it since birth. I should like to see a..." (a different one each time) "...Have you one? Don't fetch one. Either you have, or the wish passes."

success.text: She names one, then another, then a third, in case.

choices.label: Let her look at your lead.

success.text: She doesn't clap. She looks at it for a while. "That one I shan't get bored of. Odd." From the bottom of the bag: a Master Ball, "a sort of paperweight."
She waves you off with the parasol.

events.name: The Lady of the Resort: The Wish
events.intro: Selphy, waiting, the parasol tilted.

success.text: She claps, once, properly. Selphy: "Yes. Look at it. It's exactly as ridiculous as I'd hoped. Sebastian! My bag." She's no idea what any of it's worth.
She claps, once, properly. Selphy: "Yes. Look at it. It's exactly as ridiculous as I'd hoped. Sebastian! My bag." She's no idea what any of it's worth.
She claps, once, properly. Selphy: "Yes. Look at it. It's exactly as ridiculous as I'd hoped. Sebastian! My bag." She's no idea what any of it's worth.
"Then the wish passes."

events.name: The Water Labyrinth
events.intro: A reef with one hut. Captain Tidewell slows without being asked. "He'll want to look at yours. Let him. Don't talk. He hates talk." A man on the rock. He looks at your lead. Not at you. A long time. The sea goes in and out. Your lead looks back at him, and then, checking, up at you.

success.text: He nods. He goes into the hut. He comes out with something wrapped in his own coat: an Egg he's been keeping warm. "It looked up at you. To see if you were all right with me. That's all I check."

effects.text: The man on the reef gave you an Egg, because your lead looked up at you.

success.text: "Come back when it looks at you differently." He means it: on any later crossing, he looks again.

events.name: The Last Ferry

remembers.notice: On the dock: Celio, with a cable still round his neck, waving with both arms.
Lostelle, on her father's shoulders. He's got both hands on her ankles. He isn't wiping anything.
The dock's empty. Captain Tidewell: "Quiet trip. Nothing wrong with quiet."

events.intro: The ferry back. Who's on the dock depends on what was done.

success.text: Faces, and the haze behind them.
He turns the boat round without a word.

events.name: The Last Ferry: The Dock

remembers.notice: Old Winter. She doesn't wave. She's there. The Dewgong waves for her.
The boy from the Pillar, with a bottle.
A parasol, at the back, pretending to be passing.

events.intro: Further along.

success.text: The rope comes in.

events.name: The Last Ferry: Away

remembers.notice: Miss Quoyle's shut the shop to come. There's a sign on it: BACK IN TEN. SEEING OFF A REASON.

events.intro: The islands go down into the haze, one at a time, last first. The mainland comes up out of it. Captain Tidewell: "Sand in everything?"

success.text: Captain Tidewell: "Aye. That's how it gets you." A full rest. The Notebook gains a page: every island visited, and one line for each person helped.

effects.text: Took the last ferry back from the Sevii Islands, with sand in everything.
